issues.sym: The oil level drops between changes, sometimes a quart every 1,000 miles or less. You may see blue smoke at startup, and if it runs low the engine can knock or seize, often without an oil light first.
issues.why: The pistons and rings on this 2.4L engine let oil past into the cylinders, where it burns. Toyota's ZE7 warranty program covered 2008-2015 xB models and replaced the pistons on affected engines, but that coverage has now ended.
issues.next: Check the dipstick at every fill-up and top it off. Ask a shop for an oil consumption test, and ask a Toyota dealer whether your car ever got the ZE7 repair. The lasting fix is new pistons and rings or a replacement engine.

issues.sym: No warning sign before a crash. Some owners were told not to let anyone ride in the front passenger seat until the repair was done.
issues.why: These cars use Takata passenger airbag inflators. After years of heat and humidity the propellant can break down, and the inflator can burst in a crash and throw metal fragments. Some earlier replacement inflators were recalled again.
issues.next: Check the recall with your VIN today, even if you think it was already fixed. Dealers replace the inflator or airbag for free. Don't let anyone ride in the front passenger seat until it is done.

issues.sym: A long crack, often L-shaped, appears overnight or with a loud pop while driving, with no rock chip. Some owners have had the same crack come back after replacement.
issues.why: Owners have filed many NHTSA complaints about xB windshields cracking on their own, especially on 2006 and 2008 models. Owners suspect the glass or the way it is mounted is under stress, but no recall was issued.
issues.next: Have the windshield replaced by a quality glass shop that follows Toyota's install procedure, and check whether your insurance covers glass. A crack in your line of sight should be fixed right away.

issues.sym: The steering becomes very stiff and hard to turn while driving, sometimes with a red steering warning light. It may come back after a restart and then fail again.
issues.why: These cars use electric power steering. Owners report failures of the steering control module or the steering motor assembly.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Grip the wheel firmly and pull over. Have the steering codes read; the repair is usually a new steering control module or steering column assembly.

issues.t: ABS, traction and stability lights come on
issues.sym: The ABS, traction control and VSC lights come on and stay on, often in snow, slush or rain. A few owners report the car braking by itself.
issues.why: A failing wheel speed sensor or damaged sensor wiring is the common cause. On this car the rear sensor is often only sold as part of the hub and bearing.
issues.next: The normal brakes still work, but ABS and stability control may not. Have the codes read to find which wheel sensor has failed.

issues.t: Power window switch can overheat and melt (recall)
issues.sym: The driver's power window switch feels sticky or stops working, gets hot, or gives off a burning smell or smoke.
issues.why: Uneven grease applied at the factory could let the master window switch overheat and melt, which could start a fire.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check the recall with your VIN. Dealers apply special grease or replace a damaged switch for free. Don't use the switch if it smells hot.

issues.t: Sport grille can release the hood latch (recall)
issues.sym: On cars with the optional Sport Grille, the hood may not be held by its safety catch and could fly open while driving.
issues.why: The plastic grille trim could push on the secondary hood latch and release it.
issues.next: Check the recall with your VIN. Dealers add clips to hold the grille trim away from the latch for free.

issues.t: TRD brake kit hoses can fail (recall)
issues.sym: If your car has the optional TRD big brake kit, the pedal may feel soft or stopping distances get longer.
issues.why: The brake hoses in some TRD brake kits sold as accessories could wear out over time and leak.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check the recall with your VIN. If the kit is installed, Toyota swaps it for a standard brake setup for free.

issues.t: Automatic transmission harsh shifting or failure
issues.sym: Hard or jerky shifts, slipping, delayed engagement into drive, or the transmission failing completely.
issues.why: Owners report the 4-speed automatic wearing out internally. Old or low fluid speeds up the wear.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. Have a transmission shop scan for codes before deciding between a fluid service and a rebuild or replacement.

issues.t: Manual transmission pops out of 5th gear
issues.sym: The shifter jumps out of 5th gear on the highway, especially when lifting off the gas.
issues.why: Worn parts inside the 5-speed manual transmission let the gear disengage.
issues.next: Don't hold the shifter in gear for long drives. A transmission shop will need to rebuild or replace the transmission.

issues.t: Check engine light from faulty VVT-i oil control valve
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, sometimes with a rough idle or poor acceleration. Codes often point to camshaft timing.
issues.why: The variable valve timing system relies on an oil-controlled valve. If it sticks, often because of dirty or low oil, the engine computer sets the light.
issues.next: Have the codes read and check the oil level. Cleaning or replacing the oil control valve is usually the fix.

issues.sym: On Super White cars the paint flakes or comes off in sheets, often on the roof, hood and pillars.
issues.why: Toyota issued a bulletin (S-SB-0004-19) about peeling paint on 2008-2015 xB models painted Super White, and ran a paint warranty program (ZKG) for some white colors.
issues.next: Ask a Toyota dealer with your VIN whether any paint coverage still applies. Otherwise a body shop will need to strip and repaint the panels.

issues.t: Water on the passenger floor from a clogged A/C drain
issues.sym: Wet carpet on the passenger side, water dripping under the dash after using the A/C, or a musty smell.
issues.why: The A/C drain hose can clog with debris or insect nests, so condensation backs up into the cabin. Toyota has bulletins on blocked HVAC drains for these years.
issues.next: Have the A/C drain hose cleared and the carpet dried before mold sets in. It is a quick fix.

issues.sym: The A/C blows only cool air or warm air from some vents, even with the temperature set to full cold.
issues.why: Owners report two common causes: the temperature control cable slipping out of adjustment so the blend door lets heat in, and refrigerant leaks.
issues.next: Have a shop check the temperature cable adjustment first, which is simple. If it is fine, have the A/C checked for leaks.

issues.sym: No air comes out of the vents on any fan speed, or the fan works only on some speeds, often with a squeal or rattle first.
issues.why: The heater blower motor wears out with age and mileage.
issues.next: Have the blower motor and its resistor tested. Without the fan the defroster won't work, so fix it before cold or rainy weather.

issues.t: Rear hatch handle or trim breaks
issues.sym: The outside hatch handle or the plastic garnish around it snaps, and the hatch won't open or won't close and latch properly.
issues.why: The plastic handle and latch parts on the rear hatch crack with normal use. Owners mention a Scion warranty program for this part that has since expired.
issues.next: Replace the handle or garnish. Make sure the hatch latches fully, because a hatch that won't close can let exhaust into the cabin.

issues.t: Power windows or locks stop working
issues.sym: A window won't go up or down, moves slowly, or the power locks stop working on one or more doors.
issues.why: Window motors, regulators and switches wear out on these older cars.
issues.next: Have the switch and motor tested to find which part failed. If a window is stuck down, a shop can usually raise it by hand.

issues.sym: Coolant drips at the front of the car, the coolant level drops, or the engine runs hot.
issues.why: The radiator, which has plastic end tanks, can crack and leak with age.
issues.next: Keep an eye on the coolant level and temperature gauge. Replace the radiator before the engine overheats.

issues.sym: No symptom you can feel. The tire and loading sticker on the door jamb is missing or wrong.
issues.why: Some cars were sold without the required label showing how much weight the car can carry, which could lead to overloading.
issues.next: Check the recall with your VIN. A correct label is mailed or installed for free.
